items.expectedFix: Replace with New York law and exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts located in New York County.
items.note: Arizona law is outside the playbook’s accepted governing-law jurisdictions, and no acceptable court venue is specified.
items.spanText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

items.expectedFix: Preferably delete the restriction; otherwise add general-solicitation and unsolicited-approach exceptions and measure 12 months from each person’s involvement.
items.note: The mutual 12-month restriction is limited to involved personnel but lacks exceptions for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches.
items.spanText: Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

items.expectedFix: Allow Company to terminate the Agreement and any Statement of Work on 30 days’ notice with a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund, and remove Contractor’s short-notice convenience right.
items.note: Company cannot terminate an outstanding Statement of Work for convenience, while Contractor may terminate on only 15 days’ notice between engagements.
items.spanText: At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.

items.expectedFix: Permit Company assignment to affiliates and M&A successors without consent, while requiring Company consent for Contractor assignments and prohibiting assignment to a Company competitor.
items.note: The mutual consent requirement lacks affiliate and M&A-successor assignment exceptions for Company and permits Contractor assignment with consent without a competitor restriction.
items.spanText: Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.

items.expectedFix: Add at least $2 million cyber/privacy coverage, a $2 million CGL aggregate and preferably $2 million E&O coverage, with certificates on request.
items.note: Insurance is required, but the clause omits cyber/privacy coverage and does not specify the preferred CGL aggregate or E&O limit.
items.spanText: Throughout the term of this Agreement, Contractor shall maintain workers compensation insurance in the amount required by statute, comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services by Contractor pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. At Company's request, Contractor shall provide Company with certificates or other acceptable evidence of insurance or self-insurance evidencing the above coverage and shall provide Company with prompt written notice of any material change.

items.expectedFix: Insert Contractor indemnities for third-party IP claims, legal violations, Contractor-caused data breaches, gross negligence and wilful misconduct, with standard defense procedures and IP remedies.
items.note: The agreement contains no operative Contractor defense or indemnity despite the Paragraph 7 heading.

items.expectedFix: Add up to six months of transition assistance, machine-readable data return within 30 days and certified deletion thereafter.
items.note: No post-termination transition assistance, Company Data export or certified deletion obligation is provided.

items.expectedFix:
Use a mutual cap equal to the greater of 12 months’ fees paid or payable and $1,000,000, with the required uncapped carve-outs.
Replace it with the greater of 12 months’ fees paid or payable and $1,000,000 and add uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, indemnity, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement.
Add the required exceptions to the damages exclusion for confidentiality, data protection, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement.
Adopt the playbook’s mutual cap and carve-outs and clarify that Company’s undisputed payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap.
items.note:
Contractor’s cap is limited to fees paid for the particular Services and lacks the required confidentiality, security, indemnity, misconduct, fraud and IP carve-outs.
The Vendor cap may be substantially below the required 12-month-fee baseline and contains only an irrelevant Paragraph 9 carve-out.
The mutual consequential-damages exclusion has no exceptions for confidentiality, security, indemnification, misconduct, fraud or IP infringement.
Company’s cap is not integrated into the required mutual 12-month-fee structure and does not clarify that payment obligations are not damages.
items.spanText: EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES.
